spec_match.rationale: The appendHTML() column is badged 'safe' but its injector silently falls back to raw innerHTML += when appendHTML is absent (source line ~133), so on this build the cell shows the onerror attribute embedded while still labelled SAFE — misleading in exactly the browsers most visitors use.

interactive.rationale: Ten payload buttons plus 'Inject into all methods' fire real payloads; setHTML() genuinely sanitized ( retained, handler stripped) in the driven run.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Delivers the promised side-by-side injection comparison across the insertion paths.

edge_cases.rationale: Broad payload coverage (script, onerror, svg/onload, DSD, data: URI), but the unsupported-method fallback branch is the one edge that is mishandled.

references.rationale: No chromestatus link or external references on the page.

conformance.rationale: Feature-level suite renders honestly at 3 pass / 4 fail.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless CDP 2026-08-16: injected the onerror payload into all methods; per-method result cells and the alert log rendered; zero console errors.

accessibility.rationale: Native buttons, but injection outcomes and the XSS alert log are visual/text-only without live-region announcements.

openQuestions.title: Stop labelling the appendHTML fallback as SAFE
openQuestions.detail: inject() for appendHTML does `else el.innerHTML += html`, yet the column badge stays 'safe' and the summary table claims onerror is '✓ stripped'. On any browser without appendHTML (including this Chromium 141 session) the demo displays an unsanitized insertion under a SAFE label — on a security-education page. Detect the missing method and mark the column 'unsupported here — fallback is UNSAFE' instead.

openQuestions.title: Verify the appendHTML sanitization claim against the spec
openQuestions.detail: The verdict text asserts appendHTML() 'sanitizes event handlers in Chrome 151+'. The renewed-insertion proposal makes the positional methods parse like insertAdjacentHTML (no script execution) but sanitization is setHTML's job — this claim needs checking against the WHATWG PR before Chrome 151 users read it as gospel.

guidanceConsulted.query: review pass: accessible live output, honest capability fallbacks, keyboard operability for existing concept demo
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Verify semantic controls, live-region announcements for async state, visible focus, and honest unsupported states rather than fake success.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Review-only critique (no frontend change shipped with it): the rubric applied this guidance as the review bar; the page itself was not modified.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Headless-Chrome CDP drive of the page's controls on 2026-08-16 with console/network capture.

summary: Driven headless 2026-08-16: fired the onerror payload at all methods — setHTML sanitized correctly, but the appendHTML column showed the raw onerror attribute embedded (silent innerHTML+= fallback) while still badged SAFE; zero console errors. The false-safe labelling is the page's one serious defect.
